result.title: RePT: 3D Geometry Emerges from 2D Relational Pretraining
result.summary: Learning spatial representations often relies on explicitly predicting geometric quantities, but how physical geometry is organized within learned representations remains less understood. We ask whether 3D structure can emerge from learning relations across 2D observations, without 3D prediction targets. We introduce RePT, which learns compact relations between distinct physical points through cross-view 2D point prediction. The learned relation space develops a geometric organization in which magnitudes, angles, and neighborhoods reflect physical 3D displacement. A single linear readout fitted on 16 scenes recovers displacement length and angle on 39 held-out scenes without refitting (Pearson r = 0.72 and 0.78). The ARKitScenes-trained checkpoint also retains strong geometric organization on ScanNet++, showcasing generalizability. In controlled comparisons, distinct-point relational prediction consistently yields stronger geometric organization than matched same-point correspondence learning. This organization depends on additive relations and adaptive scene context, and higher point-transfer accuracy does not by itself produce stronger organization. More broadly, our results suggest that 3D geometry need not be an explicit prediction target and can instead emerge as a structural property of representations trained to relate 2D observations, pointing to relational prediction as a complementary route to learning the representations that spatial intelligence builds on.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 RePT，用跨视角 2D 点预测学习不同物理点之间的紧凑关系表示，不设 3D 预测目标；结果显示该关系空间自发形成与真实三维位移一致的几何组织，且单一线性读出可跨场景迁移。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「不显式预测也能在潜空间形成几何结构」及「点迁移准确率更高不等于组织更强」的发现，可能为 LVR 中视觉任务必要信息是否保留、训练目标如何塑造 latent 表示几何及代理指标与结构解耦的核查提供参照。
